title: Stafford's conjecture: abstract, Sections 1, 2, 7 and the appendix, paper beside Lean

generator.note: v2/extract.mjs and v2/build.mjs at this commit produce extraction.json and the reader.

paper.quote: We prove that over a Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic zero

entries.note: Lean proves the two claims of the first two sentences; the remaining sentences outline Sections 3 to 6 and are mapped there.
Lean defines A_n(k) as the free algebra on x_i, ∂_i modulo the commutator relations given by the standard symplectic matrix; PresentedWeyl is the same algebra.

UniversalStatement requires d ≠ 0, as the paper quotes the conjecture. The implication to stable cyclicity, which the paper attributes to Stafford, is proved in Lean (corollary_6_3_stablyCyclic, through the printed proof of Corollary 6.3), not cited.

PaperTheorem_1_1 is the printed statement: the span form, the identity form and, for n ≥ 1, F = Φ_{g⁻¹}(x₁)^{deg_B d} with g in the symplectic group (g J gᵀ = J); the moreover clause is stated in identity form. The paper-route proofs are theorem_1_1 and theorem_1_1_fixedSource (Section 6, outside this part); theorem_1_1 of the Challenge assembles them. The paper's own Lean reference below the theorem names Stafford38.universalStatement in FoundationClosure.lean, a separate assembly that does not go through Stafford38.Paper.
Outline of Sections 3 to 6; each claim is mapped at the environment it summarizes.

entries.note: Results of other authors, cited; not formalized here.

paper.quote: In the same paper, Stafford states the Conjecture 3.8

entries.note: Report on Stafford 1978. The identification with Theorem 1.1 and the stable cyclicity are the Lean statements shown with the paragraph on Conjecture 3.8; the monomial case is an instance of Theorem 1.1 with no separate Lean statement; the case n = 1 through the restricted minimum condition is not formalized.
Results of other authors, cited; not formalized here.

Claims about the formalization, checked outside this view: at the pinned Lean commit, #print axioms in Solution.lean reports propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for every compared theorem, and lake-manifest.json pins AlgebraicAnalysis at its tag v0.3.3.
Convention. Lean writes a right A_n(k)-module as a module over A_n(k)ᵐᵒᵖ, so m·a is op a • m, and a right ideal as a submodule of the regular right module.
Right modules are modules over A_n(k)ᵐᵒᵖ. IsCyclicModule is the same notion in the Mathlib-only statements.
Lean indexes the paper's A_n(k), n ≥ 1, as PresentedWeyl k (n + 1), and proves the stated relations and the normal form instead of citing them.
Lean indexes the filtration by ℕ with F_{-1} = 0 implicit, and defines the degree and symbol for every element, the paper only for a ≠ 0.
Lean defines both filtrations as spans of ordered PBW words of bounded weight and proves gr A_n(k) ≅ k[x, ξ] (cited by the paper).

paper.quote: For a finitely generated right $A_n$-module $M$ with a good order filtration

entries.note: Restates Definition 2.4 for the order filtration, with gr A_n(k) = k[x, ξ] as above; IsGoodFiltration is shown at Definition 2.4.
Lean takes T*X to be Spec k[x, ξ] and states the projection and fibres on closed points K^{2n}.
Lean proves the independence of the good filtration that the paper cites from [HTT, Lemma D.3.1].
Lean states Gabber's theorem for a good order filtration of a finitely generated module and proves it; theorem_2_11_cyclic is the case A_n(K)/I used later.

paper.quote: also proves the following consequences, which have no printed proof

entries.note: Left modules are Module A_n(k) M. Finite-order differential operators are k-linear endomorphisms killed by N+1 iterated commutators with multiplications (Grothendieck); "localizations" are all B with IsLocalization S B for a submonoid S of k[x₁,…,xₙ]; Laurent coefficients are the localization at x₁⋯xₙ. In the evolutionary identity k is a field of characteristic zero, the convention of Section 2, and the Lean proof uses neither Theorem 1.1 nor Section 5.
